_comment: The set §12.6 actually names: canvas-heavy apps, WebGL, audio processing,
font-dependent layouts. This is where Phase 4 breakage will be, because a
top-sites list is mostly news, login walls and CDN infrastructure that never
'surfaces' records which instrumented surface each entry is here to exercise,
so a failure can be read against the per-surface mask rather than blamed on
the whole feature. 'why' must say what would visibly break, not just what the
site is — an entry nobody can judge the failure of is not a test.
'manual' entries CANNOT be judged by the automated harness (it cannot tell
that an exported PNG is corrupt or a chart is subtly wrong). They are the
shortlist for the manual pass §12.6 requires.

sites.why: Full image editor. getImageData is load-bearing, not a fingerprint probe: filters, selections and export all read pixels back. If noise corrupts a real editing pipeline it shows here first. NOT AUTOMATABLE as of 2026-08-19: photopea.com now serves a marketing landing page and the editor boots only behind a click; the documented #{json} hash API did not launch it either (verified, canvases=[]). So run 1 tested NOTHING here. MANUAL ONLY: click through to the editor, open an image, apply a filter, export a PNG, confirm it opens.

Control for A/B DIFFERENCING, not for silence. Measured 2026-08-19: it requests /cdn-cgi/challenge-platform with the flag OFF, i.e. Cloudflare instrumentation is part of its normal load. So a raw signal count is meaningless here and only a signal present in the ON arm alone counts. If this ever appears as an A/B difference, the detector has become noisy.
PDF.js renders every page to a canvas and reads back for text selection and printing. Font-dependent as well. MANUAL: scroll pages, select text, check glyphs are not mangled.

WebGL scene using extensions. §6.5 WITHHOLDS twelve extensions (WEBGL_debug_shaders, compressed textures, EXT_disjoint_timer_query, KHR_parallel_shader_compile, OVR_multiview2, WEBGL_multi_draw). Withholding a compressed-texture extension a renderer depends on is the most plausible real breakage in all of Phase 4. MANUAL: confirm the scene renders and animates.
Heavier WebGL with texture compression paths; second opinion on the withheld-extension risk.
Chart library drawing to canvas 2D. Charts are the classic 'looks fine but is subtly wrong' case. MANUAL: compare a rendered chart against the documented sample.
D3 canvas renderers plus heavy text measurement.
Map tiles composited and read back; maps are canvas-heavy and visually unforgiving.
AnalyserNode is exactly what §6.5 perturbs. Perturbation must break the fingerprint hash WITHOUT altering audible output. MANUAL: confirm audio sounds normal and the visualiser still tracks it.
Second audio path: live analysis driving a visualiser.
Font-dependent layout with heavy measureText. §6.5 names font probing as a surface that is NOT yet instrumented, so this is also the control proving that gap is still open.

Image compressor that does canvas work IN A WORKER. Dedicated workers are perturbed and must agree with their document; this is the real-world version of the #93 browsertest. Run 1 loaded the app shell only (drop-target screen, no image processed), so the worker pipeline was NOT exercised. MANUAL: drop an image, compress, confirm the output is not corrupted.

Adversarial control, not a breakage case. A fingerprinting probe that reports the values it reads, so it proves the flag is actually taking effect end to end. Its canvas signature MUST differ between the two arms; if it does not, the whole run is invalid.
Second adversarial control, in case the first changes its reporting format.
